name: SonarQube
category: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) & Code Quality Platform
purpose: Continuous automated static code analysis to detect security vulnerabilities, security hotspots, code smells, and software bugs directly in source code repositories.
requirements: CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-04, CRA-REQ-TECH-05, CRA-REQ-TECH-06, CRA-REQ-TECH-08, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-TECH-11, CRA-REQ-TECH-12, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-DOC-01
capabilities: Deep pattern matching and AST analysis across 30+ languages; detects OWASP Top 10, SANS/CWE Top 25, hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, path traversal, weak crypto ciphers, and insecure deserialization. Enforces Quality Gates in pull requests.
limitations: Lacks dynamic runtime context; cannot detect third-party binary/library vulnerabilities (needs SCA); cannot verify operational host configuration or network encryption; cannot generate SBOMs; cannot prove non-exploitability in running application.
integrations: Git repositories (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket), CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), IDE plugins (SonarLint), Quality Gate webhook enforcement.
evidence: SonarQube Quality Gate Status Reports; Static Code Vulnerability Scan Summaries; Security Hotspot Review Logs; Technical Debt & Code Cleanliness Metrics (Annex VII dossier inputs).
complementary: Coverity (for deep memory safety / safety-critical static analysis); Black Duck / Nexus IQ (for open source dependencies and SBOMs); Penetration testing (for business logic validation).
overlaps: Overlaps with Coverity on general SAST rules and secret detection; SonarQube is faster and developer-centric, while Coverity provides deeper interprocedural taint analysis.
gaps: Zero coverage of third-party open-source SBOMs, deployed configurations, network attack surfaces, incident reporting, or post-market CVE correlation.

name: Nexus IQ Lifecycle / Nexus IQ CLM
category: Software Composition Analysis (SCA) & Open Source Governance Platform
purpose: Automated identification of open-source software (OSS) components, vulnerable third-party dependencies, license compliance risks, and automated policy enforcement across the SDLC.
requirements: CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-VULN-01, CRA-REQ-VULN-02, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-MGT-02, CRA-REQ-MGT-04, CRA-REQ-DOC-01
lifecycle: Development, Build and Release, Maintenance and RUN
capabilities: Scans package managers (Maven, npm, PyPI, NuGet, Go, etc.) for direct and transitive dependencies; provides Sonatype proprietary vulnerability intelligence and precise CVE mapping; automates pull-request dependency remediation; enforces build break policies.
limitations: Analyzes third-party dependencies only; cannot inspect first-party custom source code; cannot analyze compiled C/C++ closed-source firmware without package metadata; cannot assess runtime host hardening or network exposure.
integrations: Nexus Repository Manager / Artifactory, CI/CD plugins (Jenkins, GitLab, GitHub Actions), IDE extensions, Jira ticket automation.
evidence: Nexus IQ Policy Compliance Reports; Bill of Materials (BoM) exports (CycloneDX / SPDX); Open Source License Risk Audits; Component Vulnerability Triage Logs.
complementary: SonarQube / Coverity (for custom source code SAST); Dependency-Track (for continuous post-market SBOM lifecycle tracking); Black Duck (for deep binary snippet matching).
overlaps: Overlaps directly with Black Duck on open-source SCA and with Dependency-Track on component vulnerability tracking.
gaps: Does not perform static analysis of custom code; cannot perform dynamic penetration testing; does not provide statutory CSIRT/ENISA incident reporting.

name: Penetration Testing
category: Offensive Security Assessment & Ethical Hacking Activity / Process
purpose: Comprehensive manual and automated offensive evaluation of running product builds, deployed appliances, APIs, and cloud backends to identify exploitable security flaws and verify defensive controls.
requirements: CRA-REQ-GEN-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-02, CRA-REQ-TECH-03, CRA-REQ-TECH-04, CRA-REQ-TECH-05, CRA-REQ-TECH-06, CRA-REQ-TECH-08, CRA-REQ-TECH-09, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-TECH-11, CRA-REQ-TECH-12, CRA-REQ-TECH-13, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-VULN-07, CRA-REQ-MGT-01, CRA-REQ-DOC-01
lifecycle: Development, Build and Release, Deployment and Delivery, Maintenance and RUN
capabilities: Evaluates complex multi-step attack chains, business logic flaws, authentication/authorization bypasses (IDOR/BOLA), cryptographic protocol implementation, anti-tampering, denial-of-service resilience, and physical/logical reset mechanisms.
limitations: Point-in-time snapshot assessment; heavily reliant on assessor skill and defined testing scope; cannot continuously monitor post-release without repeated engagements; does not produce machine-readable SBOMs or formal legal DoCs.
integrations: Staging/pre-production environments, dedicated testing hardware/appliances, test tenant credentials, threat model documentation inputs.
evidence: Formal Penetration Testing Reports (Executive Summary & Technical Vulnerability Findings); Exploitation Proof-of-Concept (PoC) records; Remediation Retest Verification Certificates (Annex VII evidence).
complementary: TARA / Threat Modeling (defines penetration testing scope and focus); SAST & SCA (filters baseline bugs prior to pentest); DAST (automates repetitive web/API crawling).
overlaps: Overlaps with DAST (Burp/ZAP) on web application flaw identification; overlaps with Nessus on exposed service discovery, but with deep exploitation capability.
gaps: Cannot replace continuous automated CI/CD gating; does not generate SBOMs; cannot monitor post-market fleet without re-contracting.

name: Vulnerability Scanning (Nessus / Cyberwatch)
category: Infrastructure, Network, Host & Container Vulnerability Management Platform
purpose: Automated network service discovery, operating system vulnerability scanning, container image inspection, and CIS benchmark / hardening configuration auditing.
requirements: CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-02, CRA-REQ-TECH-04, CRA-REQ-TECH-05, CRA-REQ-TECH-08, CRA-REQ-TECH-09, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-TECH-11, CRA-REQ-TECH-12, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-MGT-04, CRA-REQ-DOC-01
lifecycle: Build and Release, Deployment and Delivery, Maintenance and RUN
capabilities: Scans exposed network daemons, operating system patch levels, and misconfigurations; audits CIS Benchmark compliance for Linux/Windows; detects default credentials, outdated SSL/TLS ciphers, and unpatched CVEs in host services. Cyberwatch adds agent-based continuous monitoring.
limitations: Network/OS level focus; cannot inspect application source code syntax or internal logic (needs SAST); cannot test custom web application business workflows or complex API auth (needs DAST/pentest); does not generate software component SBOMs.
integrations: Container registries, hypervisors, cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure), SIEM platforms, ticketing systems (Jira/ServiceNow).
evidence: Host Vulnerability Scan Reports (Nessus XML/PDF); CIS Benchmark Configuration Compliance Scores; Cyberwatch Continuous Monitoring Asset Dashboards; Patch Verification Logs.
complementary: SonarQube / Coverity (for source code bugs); Nexus IQ / Black Duck (for third-party library dependencies); Penetration testing (for active exploitation verification).
overlaps: Overlaps with Burp/ZAP on SSL/TLS and exposed web port detection; overlaps with Black Duck on container base image scanning.
gaps: Zero source code visibility; cannot evaluate application-level threat models or generate product SBOMs; cannot draft Annex II documentation.

name: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
category: Privacy Governance & Regulatory Risk Assessment Process (GDPR Art 35)
purpose: Structured legal and technical evaluation of personal data processing operations to identify, assess, and mitigate risks to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
requirements: CRA-REQ-GEN-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-04, CRA-REQ-TECH-05, CRA-REQ-TECH-06, CRA-REQ-TECH-07, CRA-REQ-TECH-12, CRA-REQ-TECH-13, CRA-REQ-MGT-01, CRA-REQ-DOC-01
lifecycle: Presales and Product Planning, Development, Maintenance and RUN
capabilities: Assesses personal data flows, processing proportionality, legal basis, data minimisation (Annex I(1)(g)), storage limitation, user consent mechanisms, user telemetry opt-out, and right-to-erasure workflows.
limitations: Governance and privacy process mandated under GDPR Art 35, NOT a technical testing tool. Does NOT evaluate technical product cybersecurity, network resilience, buffer overflows, or general software vulnerabilities under CRA.
integrations: Data Protection Officer (DPO) governance, product requirement specifications, privacy registers, GDPR Art 30 processing records.
evidence: Formal DPIA Assessment Dossier (approved and signed by DPO); Data Processing Register; Privacy Architecture Blueprint; User Consent & Telemetry Configuration Specification.
complementary: Threat Analysis & Risk Analysis (TARA) (pairs cybersecurity risk with privacy impact); Penetration testing (verifies data access boundary enforcement).
overlaps: Informs TARA regarding personal data asset values and confidentiality requirements; overlaps conceptually on access control and logging.
gaps: Does not replace cybersecurity risk assessment (Art 13(2)); does not test code, networks, or binaries; cannot satisfy CRA technical conformity by itself.

name: Threat Analysis and Risk Analysis (TARA)
category: Foundational Security Architecture & Risk Engineering Process (STRIDE / PASTA / IEC 62443)
purpose: Systematic engineering methodology to identify operational assets, threat actors, attack vectors, vulnerabilities, and potential security impact, guiding secure-by-design architectural choices.
requirements: CRA-REQ-GEN-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-02, CRA-REQ-TECH-03, CRA-REQ-TECH-04, CRA-REQ-TECH-05, CRA-REQ-TECH-06, CRA-REQ-TECH-07, CRA-REQ-TECH-08, CRA-REQ-TECH-09, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-TECH-11, CRA-REQ-TECH-12, CRA-REQ-TECH-13, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-VULN-07, CRA-REQ-MGT-01, CRA-REQ-MGT-02, CRA-REQ-DOC-01, CRA-REQ-CONF-04
lifecycle: Presales and Product Planning, Development, Maintenance and RUN
capabilities: Models trust boundaries, external data flows, privileged execution boundaries, and threat scenarios; defines technical security controls before coding begins; provides mandatory Cybersecurity Risk Assessment for Annex VII dossier.
limitations: Analytical design and planning activity; does not inspect running code, compile software, or scan binaries; depends on implementation fidelity and must be verified by empirical testing.
integrations: Enterprise Architecture tools, threat modeling platforms (IriusRisk, Threat Dragon, Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool), Jira security epic backlogs.
evidence: Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Dossier (Annex VII point 1(b)); Threat Model Architecture Diagrams & Attack Trees; Residual Risk Acceptance Register; Security Requirements Traceability Matrix.
complementary: Penetration testing (empirically tests threat model assumptions); SAST/DAST/SCA (verifies that mitigation controls are implemented correctly).
overlaps: Informs penetration testing scoping; pairs with DPIA on data flow risk analysis.
gaps: Cannot verify implementation defects without testing tools; does not generate SBOMs; cannot monitor post-market CVE feeds automatically.

name: Dependency-Track (OWASP)
category: Continuous Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) Analysis & Vulnerability Platform
purpose: Ingests CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs to provide continuous, real-time post-market vulnerability monitoring, license compliance tracking, and exploitability analysis (VEX).
requirements: CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-VULN-01, CRA-REQ-VULN-02, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-MGT-02, CRA-REQ-MGT-04, CRA-REQ-DOC-01, CRA-REQ-DOC-04
lifecycle: Build and Release, Deployment and Delivery, Maintenance and RUN
capabilities: Ingests standard SBOMs; continuously correlates component inventories against NVD, GitHub Advisories, OSV, and Sonatype OSS Index; tracks portfolio-wide vulnerability metrics; generates and ingests VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) records; REST API-first architecture.
limitations: Does not generate SBOMs from source code directly (relies on build-time tools like cdxgen/syft); does not perform SAST or DAST; does not scan custom code or running networks.
integrations: CI/CD pipelines via REST API, SBOM generation plugins (cdxgen, Maven/Gradle/npm plugins), DefectDojo, Jira/ServiceNow webhooks, NVD/OSV feeds.
evidence: Centralized Portfolio SBOM Inventory; Real-Time Vulnerability Alert Feeds; Exportable Machine-Readable SBOMs (CycloneDX JSON); VEX Exploitability Statements; Post-Market Triage Logs.
complementary: Nexus IQ / Black Duck (generates SBOMs during build); SonarQube / Coverity (covers custom code); PSIRT triage runbooks.
overlaps: Overlaps with Black Duck and Nexus IQ on post-build vulnerability tracking and CVE correlation; Dependency-Track excels as an independent, vendor-neutral SBOM manager.
gaps: Does not scan custom code; cannot test runtime interfaces or configurations; does not handle statutory incident reporting to CSIRTs/ENISA.

name: Black Duck (Synopsys / Black Duck Software)
category: Enterprise Software Composition Analysis (SCA) & Binary Analysis Platform
purpose: Comprehensive open-source discovery, deep snippet matching, binary analysis without source code, SBOM generation, license governance, and continuous CVE tracking.
requirements: CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-VULN-01, CRA-REQ-VULN-02, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-MGT-02, CRA-REQ-MGT-04, CRA-REQ-DOC-01, CRA-REQ-DOC-04
lifecycle: Development, Build and Release, Deployment and Delivery, Maintenance and RUN
capabilities: Deep signature and code snippet scanning to detect hidden/copied open source; binary analysis identifying components in compiled firmware/executables; enterprise SBOM generation (SPDX, CycloneDX); automated policy gates; continuous post-release CVE alerts.
limitations: Focuses on third-party and open source components; cannot detect custom business logic flaws in proprietary source code (needs Coverity); cannot verify dynamic web endpoints (needs DAST/pentest).
integrations: CI/CD pipelines (Detect wrapper), binary repositories (Artifactory), container registries, enterprise ERP/procurement systems, Jira.
evidence: Black Duck Open Source Audit Reports; Formal SBOM Exports (SPDX 2.3 / CycloneDX 1.6); Open Source License Risk Audits; Component Vulnerability Triage Reports.
complementary: Coverity (pairs as Synopsys Polaris suite for complete code + component coverage); Penetration testing (for runtime verification); TARA (for threat modeling).
overlaps: Overlaps directly with Nexus IQ CLM on open source SCA; overlaps with Dependency-Track on SBOM tracking; Black Duck provides superior binary and snippet matching.
gaps: Does not analyze custom proprietary code defects; cannot perform dynamic penetration testing; cannot execute statutory CSIRT notifications.

name: Coverity (Synopsys Coverity)
category: Enterprise Deep Static Application Security Testing (SAST) Platform
purpose: Industrial-strength interprocedural static analysis detecting complex memory corruption, concurrency race conditions, taint-flow security flaws, and coding defects across enterprise and embedded codebases.
requirements: CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-04, CRA-REQ-TECH-05, CRA-REQ-TECH-06, CRA-REQ-TECH-08, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-TECH-11, CRA-REQ-TECH-12, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-DOC-01
capabilities: Deep interprocedural control and data flow analysis; premier detection of buffer overflows, use-after-free, double free, integer overflows, memory leaks, null pointer dereferences in C/C++; taint analysis for web frameworks (Java, C#, Go, Python); MISRA, CERT, and OWASP compliance auditing.
limitations: Resource-intensive compilation-based analysis; does not inspect third-party open-source dependency licenses (needs Black Duck); cannot evaluate running services, network protocols, or host configurations.
integrations: Compiler toolchains (GCC, Clang, MSVC, embedded cross-compilers), CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitLab, GitHub Actions), IDE plugins (Fast Desktop), Coverity Connect dashboard.
evidence: Coverity Static Analysis Quality & Security Reports; Memory Safety Defect Verification Logs; MISRA / CERT C Compliance Reports; Pre-Release Static Audit Sign-offs.
complementary: Black Duck (for open-source SCA and SBOMs); SonarQube (for rapid day-to-day developer PR checks); Penetration testing (for dynamic business logic attacks).
overlaps: Overlaps with SonarQube on source code scanning; Coverity provides far deeper interprocedural path analysis and memory safety verification for compiled languages.
gaps: Zero SCA / SBOM generation capability; cannot test runtime environments or infrastructure; does not handle post-market fleet monitoring.

name: OWASP ZAP / Burp Suite
category: Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) & Interactive API Security Tool
purpose: Automated and interactive black-box and gray-box dynamic security testing of running web applications, REST/GraphQL APIs, and WebSocket communication channels.
requirements: CRA-REQ-TECH-01, CRA-REQ-TECH-02, CRA-REQ-TECH-04, CRA-REQ-TECH-05, CRA-REQ-TECH-06, CRA-REQ-TECH-08, CRA-REQ-TECH-09, CRA-REQ-TECH-10, CRA-REQ-VULN-03, CRA-REQ-DOC-01
lifecycle: Development, Build and Release, Deployment and Delivery
capabilities: Active/passive scanning of running endpoints; intercepts and manipulates HTTP/S traffic; identifies injection flaws (SQLi, XSS, SSRF), authentication/session bypasses, insecure direct object references (IDOR), security header misconfigurations, and API rate limiting weaknesses.
limitations: Requires a running, testable target instance; limited visibility into internal source code logic, database structures, or memory state; cannot scan closed-source binaries or generate SBOMs; cannot monitor post-market fleets continuously.
integrations: Staging environments, OpenAPI / Swagger specifications, Postman collections, CI/CD pipelines (ZAP automation framework), DefectDojo, Jira.
evidence: DAST Automated Scan Reports (HTML/JSON); Burp Suite Professional / Enterprise Assessment Dossiers; API Security Vulnerability Logs; HTTP Security Header Audit Records.
complementary: SonarQube / Coverity (SAST finds internal code flaws while DAST finds exposed endpoint flaws); Penetration testing (human tester uses Burp for complex exploits).
overlaps: Overlaps with manual penetration testing (Burp is the primary tool used by pentest consultants); overlaps with Nessus on web server header checks.
gaps: Cannot inspect source code or firmware internals; cannot generate SBOMs; cannot verify legal compliance or incident reporting.
